original_card.question: Can one reproducible environment or artifact-comparison failure be repaired?
methods: Reproduce one portability failure and add a minimal cross-environment fix.
Audit one canonical-payload comparison for omitted proof-relevant fields.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Preserve immutable source hashes and proof-relevant content; a different compressed byte stream alone is not a mathematical mismatch.

first_step.inspect: Read the gzip-container reproducibility examples and distinguish frozen source bytes from regenerated payloads.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Reproduce one specific mismatch or audit one canonical comparison for omitted proof-relevant fields.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Portable exact checks prevent environment failures from blocking valid contributions.
allowed_variations: One interpreter/version mismatch or one payload field comparison.
scope_change_triggers: Removing immutable-source pins because generated compressed bytes differ.

actual_scope: Interpreter matrix (CPython 3.10-3.14, five PYTHONHASHSEED settings, macOS arm64) for the selected #1094 record's only post-#1042 stage, research/complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges/verify.py, run from the hash-bound archived #1042 slots/local, with a file-by-file byte and canonical-payload comparison against the reviewed run archived in research/community-frontier1094-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one portability failure or one canonical-payload comparison; this picks the selected record's final stage as the object and checks whether any interpreter or hash seed changes its output payload, and which receipt fields are inherently non-reproducible. No failure was found to repair, so the result is a portability receipt plus a reusable comparison tool rather than a fix.
bottleneck_link: Side result for review throughput: shows a reviewer can rerun the selected final stage on any CPython 3.10-3.14 and expect byte-identical artifacts apart from one relocated path map and timings, and identifies the one #1094 receipt hash (outer stage log) that no rerun can reproduce.
stop_rule: One stage, one platform, five interpreters; no cold #1042/#799 rebuild and no edit to selected or frozen scripts.
evidence: All 5 interpreters and 5 hash-seed runs pass with kappa 0.001672660197076918; of 105 outputs, 102 are byte-identical to the reviewed run (all 22 .gz, all 11 inner logs), INDEPENDENT-T16.json is equal after relocating absolute path keys, REPLAY.json/STAGES.json differ only in 11 'seconds' values. verify.py reruns the stage (~20 s) and checks this classification plus seven negative controls.
author: JosieElliston (donated Claude Code session 26, Claude Opus 5.5)
ai_assistance: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the scripts and text in JosieElliston's donated session 26; self-reviewed only, no independent AI or human review.

open_questions.question: Does the same byte-level agreement hold on Linux (Ubuntu CI, Python 3.12) and Windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Then a cross-OS reviewer could compare receipts directly instead of rerunning.
open_questions.first_step: Run verify.py on Ubuntu with Python 3.12.
open_questions.blocked_by: No Linux host in this session.

open_questions.question: Should the #1094 receipt drop or annotate its non-reproducible outer log_sha256 (the stage log prints wall-clock seconds)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Makes two runs' receipts directly comparable.
open_questions.first_step: Maintainer decision; this package changes no selected script.
open_questions.blocked_by: Any edit to scripts/verify_frontier1094.py touches the selected reproduction path.

open_questions.question: Do the #1042 stages' 457 bound artifacts reproduce byte for byte across interpreters?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Would let reuse mode be checked against the published receipt on another machine.
open_questions.first_step: Run compare_payloads.py on a cold verify_frontier1042.py run against community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz.
open_questions.blocked_by: A cold run takes about 20 minutes plus the #799 baseline.
